target.title: fix(voice-call): redact phone numbers in event logs via subsystem logger
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The voice-call channel was logging raw phone numbers to console in `events.ts` (`shouldAcceptInbound` and `createWebhookCall`). Unlike all other channels (WhatsApp, Slack, Discord, Signal, Telegram, etc.) which use `createSubsystemLogger` → tslog → file transport with `redactSecrets` + `redactSensitiveText` double redaction, voice-call used bare `console.log` with no PII protection.

A survey of the codebase confirmed voice-call is the sole outlier with 143 bare `console.*` calls across 17 files, while other channels have 0–3 non-PII console calls each.

## Why This Change Was Made

Align the `events.ts` logger surface with the established channel pattern. Phone numbers are PII and should never appear in plaintext in log output.

## User Impact

- Phone numbers logged from `events.ts` are now SHA256-hashed via `redactIdentifier()`, producing stable but irreversible identifiers (`sha256:b275013166a6`)
- Logs now route through the `SubsystemLogger` (`voice-call/events`) instead of bare `console.*`, which means they benefit from:
  - File transport for persistence (previously console-only)
  - Subsystem-level log filtering
  - Automatic `redactSensitiveText()` pass at the transport boundary
- The `[voice-call]` prefix is dropped from log messages — the subsystem logger adds its own structured subsystem metadata

## Evidence

### Real runtime redacted output

Standalone script exercising the same `createSubsystemLogger("voice-call/events")` + `redactIdentifier()` code path with representative phone numbers:

```
$ node --import tsx scripts/voice-call-redact-proof.mjs

=== Redacted voice-call event log output ===

[voice-call/events] Inbound call accepted: caller=sha256:b275013166a6 allowlisted=true
[voice-call/events] Inbound call rejected: caller=sha256:cb6880e41676 allowlisted=false
[voice-call/events] Inbound call rejected: caller=sha256:ec61f3c620a9 allowlisted=false
[voice-call/events] Created inbound call record: a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890 caller=sha256:b275013166a6
[voice-call/events] Inbound call rejected by policy but no provider to hang up (providerCallId: pcall-123, caller=sha256:ec61f3c620a9); call will time out on provider side.
[voice-call/events] Failed to reject inbound call pcall-456: connection refused

=== End of redacted log output ===
```

Observations:
- All raw phone numbers replaced by `sha256:` stable hash identifiers — no plaintext PII in output
- Same phone number maps to same hash across calls (`+15550001234` → `sha256:b275013166a6` in both accepted and record-creation lines)
- `[voice-call/events]` subsystem tag added automatically by the logger, removing need for manual `[voice-call]` prefix
- Messages without PII (e.g. `Failed to reject inbound call`) pass through unmodified
- No `console.log`/`console.warn` calls remain in `events.ts`

### Tests

- 19/19 tests pass in `extensions/voice-call/src/manager/events.test.ts`
- Branch rebased on current `origin/main` (commit `930472bd3b304`)

### References

- WhatsApp channel pattern in `extensions/whatsapp/src/send.ts` using `redactIdentifier()` + `createSubsystemLogger()`
- Subsystem logger redacts messages before console output: `src/logging/subsystem.ts:271`
- No other channel uses bare `console.log` for production logging

### What was not tested

- Live voice-call flow with real Twilio/Telnyx carrier webhook (requires real provider setup with phone number provisioning)

Behavior addressed: raw phone numbers removed from all voice-call event log output
Real environment tested: standalone script exercising the exact same subsystem logger + redactIdentifier path used in production
Exact steps: `node --import tsx scripts/voice-call-redact-proof.mjs`
Observed result after fix: all phone numbers replaced by sha256: hashes in console output; subsystem metadata prefix present
